summary: Only Hacker News was reachable today (Reddit, X, Bluesky and others were blocked), so every source below is a verified HN thread or comment from the last 7 days. The strongest themes: Microsoft silently bouncing mail from domains without DMARC, pay-by-app parking fees and flaky apps, inbox spam aimed at people who publish an email address, and SaaS price hikes (Harvest) pushing freelancers away.

ideas.title: MailGuard Watch: email-auth monitor for small domains and agencies
ideas.oneLiner: Watches SPF/DKIM/DMARC and big-provider bounce rules for every client domain, and tells you the one DNS record to add before customers' mail starts bouncing.
ideas.problem: Since 5 Nov 2026 Outlook.com/Hotmail have been rejecting some mail from domains with no DMARC record, with no announcement. Small businesses and the IT people who look after them found out when customers stopped replying. Existing DMARC tools are built for enterprises and are overkill for a 5-person business.
ideas.targetUsers: Freelance web developers, MSPs and small agencies managing 10–200 client domains; small businesses that email customers from their own domain.
ideas.monetization: Per-domain pricing, e.g. ₹99 / $2 per domain per month, with agency bundles of 25 domains for ₹1,499 / $19. Free single-domain checker as a lead magnet.
mvp: Paste a domain and get SPF, DKIM selector and DMARC status with plain-language fixes
Copy-paste DNS records for Cloudflare, GoDaddy, Namecheap and Google Domains-style hosts
Weekly re-check of all domains with email and WhatsApp alerts when a record breaks or changes
Test send to an Outlook/Gmail/Yahoo seed inbox and report whether it landed or bounced
Client-ready PDF report agencies can forward to customers

competitors.name: dmarcian
competitors.gap: Aimed at security teams; report parsing is powerful but heavy for a business that just needs to know whether its mail is being delivered.

competitors.name: EasyDMARC
competitors.gap: Pricing and dashboards are built around enterprise DMARC enforcement, not quick fixes for dozens of tiny domains.

competitors.name: MXToolbox
competitors.gap: Good one-off lookups, but no cross-client monitoring that explains provider policy changes in plain language.

ideas.title: MeterMate: find the cheapest way to pay for parking
ideas.oneLiner: A crowd-sourced map that tells you which meters accept tap-to-pay, which parking app to use, what fee each charges, and reminds you before your session ends.
ideas.problem: Cities are pushing pay-by-app parking. Users report convenience fees on every session (and again when extending), large app downloads on poor mobile data, apps that don't work in underground garages, and forced sign-ups with phone number and email. A new study found a median $0.35 fee per session across 312 US cities.
ideas.targetUsers: Daily city drivers and visitors; initially US/UK/EU cities with ParkMobile, PayByPhone, RingGo and similar apps. Indian city drivers using FASTag/municipal apps are a second market.
ideas.monetization: Free core map and timer; $2.99/mo Pro for multi-vehicle session reminders and monthly fee-savings report. Optional city/operator data licensing later.
mvp: Map pins for zones: pay-at-meter tap-to-pay available, which app operator, and the per-session fee, submitted by users
Zone number lookup by GPS so you know which app/zone code applies before downloading anything
Local session timer with push reminder before expiry and a one-tap link to extend in the right app
Saved plates and zones, offline-first so it works in underground garages
Monthly 'fees you could have avoided' summary

competitors.name: ParkMobile
competitors.gap: Charges per-session convenience fees and is one app among several per region; users cite fees and forced accounts.

competitors.name: PayByPhone
competitors.gap: Same per-transaction fee model; each city runs a different operator so people end up with several apps.

competitors.name: Parkopedia
competitors.gap: Focuses on finding garages and prices, not on avoiding payment-app fees or tracking meter alternatives.

ideas.title: KnockKnock: a contact link that filters AI cold outreach
ideas.oneLiner: Replace the email in your bio with a link that asks senders for a quick proof-of-effort or reputation check, then forwards only real humans to your inbox.
ideas.problem: People who publish an email on HN, GitHub, blogs and bios now get LLM-written 'I saw your comment' outreach, fake consulting offers and promo scams. Some give up and delete their email or shut down office-hours links; others route everything to spam and miss the real messages.
ideas.targetUsers: Developers, writers, open-source maintainers, indie founders and creators with a public email address.
ideas.monetization: Free for 1 link and 20 forwards/month; $4/month for custom domain, unlimited forwards, allow-lists and weekly digest of blocked messages.
mvp: Hosted contact page at yourname.knock.link with rate limiting and a short effort challenge instead of a plain captcha
Optional reputation check: sender links HN, GitHub or LinkedIn profile and you set minimum thresholds
Forward passing messages to your real email with a reply-through proxy address so your address is never exposed
Weekly digest of blocked messages so nothing important is lost
Embeddable snippet and plain-text-safe link for profiles

competitors.name: SimpleLogin
competitors.gap: Hides your address with aliases but does not judge whether the sender is a human with a genuine reason to write.

competitors.name: Formspree
competitors.gap: A form backend with basic spam filtering; LLM-written personalised outreach passes through.

competitors.name: Cal.com
competitors.gap: Scheduling links get abused for the same 'please do a free 30 minute call' requests.

ideas.title: FlatTime: time tracking and invoicing with no percentage cut
ideas.oneLiner: Simple hours-to-invoice tool with one flat price, no per-invoice usage fees and no skimming of your payments.
ideas.problem: After Harvest's acquisition, users report being pushed from $40/month to plans quoted at several hundred dollars, and a flex plan that takes about 2% extra on top of card fees. Free accounts lost the ability to send invoices outside the payment portal. Some freelancers are already vibe-coding their own replacements.
ideas.targetUsers: Solo consultants, small agencies and freelancers who bill by the hour, including Indian freelancers invoicing foreign clients.
ideas.monetization: Flat $6/month or ₹399/month per account with unlimited invoices and clients; a one-time $49 lifetime option. No payment-processing markup; users bring their own Stripe or Razorpay.
mvp: Timer and manual hour entry by project and client
Invoice builder with PDF export and invoice numbering, GST/VAT fields
Import from Harvest and Toggl CSV exports
Bring-your-own Stripe/Razorpay payment link, no percentage cut
Recurring retainers and overdue reminders

competitors.name: Harvest
competitors.gap: Recent pricing changes with usage fees and a processing surcharge; users describe sudden renewal jumps.

competitors.gap: Strong timer but invoicing is limited and priced by seat for teams.

competitors.name: Clockify
competitors.gap: Free tier is generous but invoicing and reports feel bolted on and paywalled for basics.

ideas.title: ReleaseSafe: automatic fallback mirror for GitHub release downloads
ideas.oneLiner: A tiny proxy and CLI that caches the release binaries your CI downloads, verifies checksums, and transparently serves them when GitHub returns 504.
ideas.problem: During the 8 Nov GitHub outage, release downloads timed out while the status page stayed green. CI pipelines that fetch tools such as gitleaks or Terraform failed, and individuals could not download installers like Rufus or distro ISOs.
ideas.targetUsers: Small dev teams and solo developers with CI that pulls binaries from GitHub Releases; DevOps engineers; Linux users bootstrapping machines.
ideas.monetization: Free self-hosted CLI; hosted mirror at $9/month per team with 20 GB cache and usage dashboard; $29/month with private-repo asset support and audit logs.
mvp: Drop-in URL rewrite or GitHub Action that fetches via the mirror first, falling back to GitHub
Pin by version plus SHA256 so the mirror can never serve a tampered file
Cache on S3-compatible or R2 storage, bring your own bucket
Config file generated by scanning your workflows for github.com/*/releases/download URLs
Slack or email alert when a download came from the fallback

competitors.name: mise / aqua
competitors.gap: Tool version managers that still download from GitHub at install time; they don't ship a managed fallback.

competitors.name: actions/cache
competitors.gap: Cache lives on GitHub's own infrastructure and misses on cold runners, so it fails exactly when GitHub is down.

competitors.name: JFrog Artifactory
competitors.gap: Does the job but is heavy and priced for large organisations.

ideas.title: RenewalRadar: catch SaaS price jumps before the invoice hits
ideas.oneLiner: Forward renewal and billing emails; get a flag when the next charge is much higher than the last one, with the plan change explained.
ideas.problem: Small teams are hit by renewal notices that jump from tens to hundreds of dollars through seat bundles, 'unlimited' re-tiering and usage fees buried behind 'starting from' pricing. They discover it at renewal, when switching is costly.
ideas.targetUsers: Freelancers, agencies and 2–50 person companies that run on a stack of per-seat SaaS tools; bookkeepers and ops managers.
ideas.monetization: Free for 5 tracked subscriptions; $5/month for unlimited tracking, price-history charts and Slack/WhatsApp alerts; $19/month for team inbox forwarding and CSV export for accountants.
mvp: Dedicated forwarding email address that parses vendor renewal and invoice emails
LLM extraction of vendor, plan, seats and amount, stored against previous charges
Alert when the upcoming amount is more than a set percentage above the last one
Calendar of renewal and notice deadlines with cancel-by reminders
Per-vendor price history and yearly total

competitors.name: Subscription trackers (Rocket Money, Bobby)
competitors.gap: Built for consumer subscriptions via bank connection; they track charges after the fact rather than parsing B2B renewal notices in advance.

competitors.name: Vendr / Zylo
competitors.gap: Enterprise SaaS-management contracts, far beyond what a 5-person team will pay.

ideas.title: BankCheck: which banking apps work on de-Googled phones
ideas.oneLiner: A live, crowd-verified compatibility database of banking and payment apps on GrapheneOS and other non-Google Android builds, with alternatives per country.
ideas.problem: Banks are adopting Play Integrity checks and rejecting privacy-focused Android builds, often only at sign-up, so users find out after installing. Some resort to a spare phone just for banking, and tap-to-pay options (Google Pay, Wero) are narrowing further.
ideas.targetUsers: Privacy-minded Android users on GrapheneOS, CalyxOS or similar; people choosing a bank or a phone; Europe first, then India (UPI app compatibility).
ideas.monetization: Free for readers; $3/month for alerts when an app you use changes status; sponsorship from privacy-friendly banks and phone resellers.
mvp: Searchable table of apps by country with status: works, works for existing accounts only, blocked at signup, blocked
One-tap user reports with OS version and date, and a freshness indicator per entry
Per-country 'banks that work' shortlist and tap-to-pay workaround notes
Email or RSS alerts when an app you follow changes status
Public API/JSON export so others can embed it

competitors.name: PrivSec banking app compatibility list
competitors.gap: A static article maintained by hand; no per-user reports, freshness indicators or alerts.
